newsitem.title: DENMARK: DANISH STATE BONDS BOOSTED BY BUBA.
newsitem.headline: DANISH STATE BONDS BOOSTED BY BUBA.

text.p: Danish government bond prices continued to firm on Tuesday in the wake of the Bundesbank's decision to keep its repo rate at a fixed three percent but mortage-backed paper was sluggish, held back by the imminent expiry of several series.

The yield spread between the seven percent 2007 state bond and the 10-year German bund inched to 59 basis points from Monday's 58 bp. At 1240 GMT the 2007 bond traded 0.28 point up from Monday to 105.57, yielding 6.24 percent .
Dealers saw the gap closing if German prices rose further, saying Danish paper had lost a disproportionate amount lately.
The outgoing benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 stood at 112.70, up 0.25 point from Monday, with the yield at 6.05 percent.
Turnover in both the 2007 and 2006 bonds was low, at 700 million crowns and 800 million respectively around midday.
The 2006's September future was untraded at 112.12 and the six percent mortgage bond due 2026 was also untraded, at 91.70.
The crown firmed to 3.8083 to the mark, from Monday's 3.8091. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +(45) 33969650
